findings.issue_text: In set_locale, I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called before I18n.locale is assigned the newly computed locale, so the wrong fallback set is preloaded and the optimization silently does nothing
FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides [] to always return a computed array, silently discarding standard fallback configuration writes like I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [:de, :en]
Mixing String and Symbol locales in the fallback array breaks uniq deduplication, causing duplicate backend lookups and double locale loading due to type-strict include? checks
Assigning I18n.fallbacks in an initializer may be overwritten by the Rails i18n railtie's after_initialize hook, reverting the custom fallback behavior
Enabling fallbacks in all environments (previously only production/profile) changes test semantics, and load-order depends on fragile filename sorting ('0' before 'i')
ensure_loaded! in translate_accelerator.rb is not thread-safe: concurrent threads can race through the check-then-load pattern, causing double-loading and interleaved writes to shared state

FallbackLocaleList#[] in config/initializers/i18n.rb rebuilds the fallback array and re-reads SiteSetting.default_locale on every translation lookup, creating hot-path recomputation that should be memoized per locale/site
set_locale in application_controller.rb runs ensure_loaded! on every request, walking the full fallback chain and eager-loading locales even for requests that render no translations

ensure_loaded! in translate_accelerator.rb does not append the locale to @loaded_locales, potentially causing locales to be re-loaded from disk on every request (and twice per request via both set_locale and translate's lazy-load path) if load_locale doesn't mutate @loaded_locales

goldens.comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

adjudication_records.issue_text: In set_locale, I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called before I18n.locale is assigned the newly computed locale, so the wrong fallback set is preloaded and the optimization silently does nothing

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` added at the very end of `set_locale`, immediately before the method `end`. There is no diff evidence that `I18n.locale` is assigned *after* this call; if anything, the surrounding `if/else ... SiteSetting.default_locale ... end` block commonly forms the RHS of an `I18n.locale = ...` assignment that would have already executed before the newly-added line. Since the finding depends on code order not shown/verified in the diff, and the insertion point is last in the method, the claim that it runs before `I18n.locale` is assigned is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides [] to always return a computed array, silently discarding standard fallback configuration writes like I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [:de, :en]

adjudication.rationale: In config/initializers/i18n.rb, FallbackLocaleList < Hash overrides `[]` to always return a computed array `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`, ignoring any values that might have been written into the underlying Hash. Since `[]=` is not overridden, assignments like `I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [...]` would store data but subsequent reads via `[]` would not return it, effectively making such configuration writes ineffective. The diff doesn’t show any actual `[]=` usage elsewhere, so the impact can’t be confirmed as a concrete defect from the diff alone, but it is a real, diff-grounded behavior/maintainability concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Assigning I18n.fallbacks in an initializer may be overwritten by the Rails i18n railtie's after_initialize hook, reverting the custom fallback behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new initializer explicitly setting `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` (config/initializers/i18n.rb) and, importantly, removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from all shown environment configs (production/profile/cloud66). Nothing in the diff indicates a Rails `after_initialize` hook is configured to reassign/overwrite `I18n.fallbacks` after this initializer runs, so the claimed overwrite/regression cannot be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Enabling fallbacks in all environments (previously only production/profile) changes test semantics, and load-order depends on fragile filename sorting ('0' before 'i')

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves fallbacks setup from `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` in specific environment files (production/profile/cloud66) to a global initializer (`config/initializers/i18n.rb`) that unconditionally includes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` and sets `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`, affecting all environments including test. Also, the initializer explicitly notes an ordering dependency (`# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb`), implying behavior depends on filename-based initializer load order (e.g., `02-...` before `i18n.rb`), which is a fragile coupling. This is a concrete review concern, though not provably a defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList#[] in config/initializers/i18n.rb rebuilds the fallback array and re-reads SiteSetting.default_locale on every translation lookup, creating hot-path recomputation that should be memoized per locale/site

adjudication.rationale: In config/initializers/i18n.rb, FallbackLocaleList#[] is overridden to compute and return a new array each time: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`. Since this method is the hash accessor used by I18n’s fallback resolution, it plausibly runs frequently during translation lookup and will re-read `SiteSetting.default_locale` and rebuild the array each call. That’s a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by this diff, but not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: set_locale in application_controller.rb runs ensure_loaded! on every request, walking the full fallback chain and eager-loading locales even for requests that render no translations

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` at the end of `set_locale` (application_controller.rb), which will run on every request. `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` (config/initializers/i18n.rb) iterates the fallback chain `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` and calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each. While `I18n.ensure_loaded!(locale)` (translate_accelerator.rb) avoids re-loading already-loaded locales via `@loaded_locales`, the fallback chain is still walked and the initial request for a locale will eagerly load fallbacks even if no translations are rendered. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/behavior concern but not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ensure_loaded! in translate_accelerator.rb does not append the locale to @loaded_locales, potentially causing locales to be re-loaded from disk on every request (and twice per request via both set_locale and translate's lazy-load path) if load_locale doesn't mutate @loaded_locales

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ensure_loaded!(locale)` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` that checks `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` but does not itself append `locale` to `@loaded_locales`. Whether this is a real reload bug depends on whether `load_locale` mutates `@loaded_locales` (not shown in the diff). As written, `ensure_loaded!` relies on that side effect; if `load_locale` doesn’t add to `@loaded_locales`, the guard is ineffective and `load_locale` could be called repeatedly (including from both `ApplicationController#set_locale` via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` and `translate`’s lazy-load path).
